name: CSS 3D staging (tilted cards, carousels, perspective floors)

source.description: Four inspected references place flat cards in perspective: a curved carousel of portrait cards, tilted UI or paper panels, letters standing on a perspective grid floor.

technique: Flat elements are arranged and moved in a CSS perspective space (rotateX/rotateY/translateZ) so they gain depth, scale and occlusion without a 3D renderer.
purpose: Depth and showcase for collections of cards, UI screens and type.
visual_behaviour: A ring of cards rotates past the camera; a panel tilts back into the frame; letters stand on a receding grid.
mechanics: preserve-3d containers, perspective on the stage, rotationY of a ring with cards at translateZ radius; motion blur at speed (see directional-smear).

decomposition.timing: Carousel turns of 1-2 s; tilts of 0.6-1 s.

failure_modes: GPU compositing differences between preview Chromium and HyperFrames
Text on tilted planes below the readability floor

implementation.approach: GSAP 3D transforms (rotationX/Y, z, transformPerspective) on DOM cards; needs a render-host check of 3D compositing in HyperFrames before a component is built.

requirements: CSS 3D transforms in the capture path
limitations: Unverified in HyperFrames on the M2

provenance.observed: Portrait video cards on a curved carousel spin with reflections.
A paper card tilts in perspective; letters stand on a receding grid floor.
A dashboard card tilts in perspective (approx., from overview spacing).
A text panel tilts back in perspective before a camera push.

licensing_notes: Technique only; use original or user-supplied card content, never reference UIs or faces.
